newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi-Italy will do what is necessary to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi-Italy will do what is necessary to join EMU.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, seeking to calm nervous markets, said on Monday that Italy would do "everything necessary to take part (in the single currency) from the start."
Commenting on the treasury's announcement that Italy intended to issue a seven-year one billion Euro-denominated bond, Ciampi said in a statement:
"We believe in the Euro. The single currency will be our currency. We will do everything that is necessary to take part in it from the start," he said.
"Even today, with the approval by ECOFIN (EU Finance ministers) of the German and French convergence plans, shows the firm will of all to carry out the project in the time envisaged.
"This too will help spread a more relaxed climate in the markets," the statement concluded.
European Union finance ministers fully backed plans by Germany and France, the two nations at the heart of European Monetary Union (EMU) to qualify for the single currency.
The ministers also reaffirmed their belief that the single currency would start on time in 1999.
Italian bonds took a hammering on Monday as investors were seized by doubts over Italy's chances of restoring its state finances to health in time.
The centre-left government has made joining EMU from the start a cornerstone of its strategy to slash a huge public sector deficit.

But investors have been unsettled by the difficulties Prime Minister Romano Prodi has been having in forging a consensus behind a supplementary budget vital to keep Italy's quest for EMU membership on track.
